https://www.dw.com/en/brics-leaders-gath.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MIIU This year's BRICS host India has to balance welcoming new members like Iran without appearing to snub the US Image: Qamar Sibtain/IANS Advertisement In preparation for hosting the 18th BRICS summit in Delhi this weekend, India came up with a slogan which tried to keep the group's brand intact without alienating its many new members. "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability" matches the acronym for the body's five original members — Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa — whilst also denoting goals which the new members — Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates — can get behind. "It's an elegant way to reinterpret BRICS so that the acronym represents a joint mission rather than country names," Mihaela Papa, director of the BRICS Lab at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, told DW. For Sushant Singh, lecturer in South Asian Studies at Yale University, the vague slogan reflects India's desire as hosts to keep BRICS as low-key and neutral as possible. "India doesn't want to offend Russia or China, but the fact is that Indians are looking more towards the United States these days. The desire to build up BRICS is not there." India takes host role Yet host India's status as a rising global geopolitical power has added clout to this year's gathering when compared with last year's summit in Brazil. At the Rio de Janeiro gathering , six of the bloc's 11 heads of state skipped the event, including major players like Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Putin is expected to attend, while Xi Jinping is widely expected but not yet formally confirmed by Beijing. "The participation of China's top leadership is crucial," says Papa. She also thinks it would be a significant sign of the BRICS' strength as a "stabilizing force" if the leaders of regional rivals Iran and the UAE were shown to be able to work together. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian will attend but UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan is expected to send representatives. Saudi Arabia, another Iranian foe, is also expected to. The country's BRICS status remains somewhat ambiguous, although current official BRICS materials generally list it as a member. Several heads of state skipped the 2025 gathering Image: Fabio Teixeira/Anadolu/picture alliance For India, the summit is as significant for the bilateral meetings it brings as much as for the BRICS gathering itself. Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi are due to meet on Friday while the summit will also present an opportunity for Xi and Modi to speak face-to-face amid continued strain in the China-India relationship. However, that does not mean much of substance will emerge from the weekend. "In terms of concrete outcomes and what is achievable, I think it's going to be very, very limited," says Singh. Modi has spoken of BRICS as an important forum for the 'Global South' to present a common front on various issues. He has also spoken about "a people-centric approach" and the spirit of "humanity first". However, Singh says BRICS is simply not a priority for India and that in general, Delhi has not appreciated what many have interpreted as the "anti-western" turn the group has taken in recent times. "With India as chair, India won't be comfortable with any kind of anti-western line," he says, pointing to the focus it places on defense ties with the US and trade ties with the west as a whole. The leaders of Russia, China and India will all be present this year Image: REUTERS/ANI "India's idea of BRICS is more to look at improving trade ties, etc. In other words, can we do things which are beneficial to us without in any way being confrontational or critical of the West?" Yet ironically, India's non-aligned status means it may actually be able to keep the bloc aligned. "India adds clout because it has significant geopolitical weight and relationships across competing camps, making it an important bridge-builder," says Papa. "Its approach is likely to keep BRICS focused on practical cooperation and global governance reform rather than overt bloc politics." What is BRICS for anyway? BRICS is soon approaching its 18th birthday, so in a sense it should be coming of age. Yet the bloc has struggled for coherence in recent years amid doubt over its purpose. The scale of what it could represent is not in doubt. It boasts nearly half the world's population among its members and around 40% of its GDP. Last year, its joint declaration called for reforms of global governance, specifying representation on multilateral bodies such as the IMF and the World Bank. It also condemned tariffs and decried what it called the "polarization" of the international order. "Ideologically, BRICS remains where it was during the last summit in Brazil, focused on practical, functional cooperation while seeking to avoid geopolitical tensions," says Papa. BRICS foreign ministers have already met ahead of the summit Image: ANI She says that the expansion of the group from five to 11 members — if we include Saudi Arabia — has made it harder to reach consensus on various issues. There are also now more autocracies among its members than democracies, while many members have tense bilateral relations. "These internal contradictions will always be hard to reconcile," says Singh. What might happen this year Nonetheless, Papa says she expects progress this year in three areas: trade, monetary cooperation, and agriculture. Discussions are likely to focus on improving trade between the members, alternative financial architecture for exchanging currencies and on issues around food security. While talk of reforming global governance will still be central, she thinks BRICS' best hope to focus on the institutions which it agrees most on. For example, India is reluctant to press for UN reform but is keen for a co-ordinated approach from BRICS to trade and the WTO. "India's WTO ambitions are shared by more members," she says, which makes movement in that area "more likely." Yet many still share Singh's view that the group will "continue to underwhelm." He says issues ranging from China's growing global dominance to the Trump administration's stance on tariffs have made the bloc's limited goals even harder to achieve. "With the kind of world that we are in and the lack of coherence and internal contradictions that BRICS has, it's very unlikely that it will achieve anything major," he says. https://ianslive.in/eam-jaishankar-calls.text: EAM Jaishankar calls on Polish President, discusses positive trajectory of Strategic Partnership IANS September 4, 2026 9:32 PM Share on | Warsaw, Sep 4 (IANS) External Affairs Minister (EAM) S Jaishankar on Friday called on Polish President Karol Nawrocki in Warsaw, holding talks on the positive trajectory of the India-Poland Strategic Partnership. “Glad to call on Polish President Karol Nawrocki. Our conversation focused on the positive trajectory of our Strategic Partnership. Exchanged views on the Ukraine conflict, Middle East/West Asia, IMEC and G20,” EAM Jaishankar stated on X. He also met the India-Poland Parliamentary Group and shared perspectives on fashioning a contemporary India-Poland relationship. “Pleased to meet with the India-Poland Parliamentary Group led by Kinga Gajewska. Shared perspectives on fashioning a contemporary India-Poland relationship. Discussed this and other regional developments in the larger context of our ties with the EU. Look forward to regular exchanges between our Parliamentary friendship groups,” EAM Jaishankar stated on X. Earlier in the day, EAM Jaishankar met Radosław Sikorski, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Poland, in Warsaw as they reviewed the progress of the Joint Action Plan 2024-28. “This afternoon, met with DPM and FM Radosław Sikorski of Poland here in Warsaw. We reviewed the progress of our Joint Action Plan 2024-28, focusing on trade and investment, space, digital, AI, semiconductors, defence, education, shipping, mining and energy, people-to-people, culture and multilateral cooperation,” EAM Jaishankar stated on X after the meeting. “Value Poland’s support for deeper India-EU cooperation. Confident that the entry into force of the FTA will lead to even closer bilateral cooperation. Discussed the complex global challenges, including supply chain resilience and food, fuel and fertiliser security. Endless war must give way to end of war,” he added. Highlighting ongoing wars, challenges of food, fuel and fertiliser availability faced by the world currently, EAM Jaishankar said that India and Poland can cooperate to shape the direction of many important global debates. Addressing media jointly with Sikorski following their talks in Warsaw, EAM Jaishankar said that they discussed some major global and regional issues, including the conflict in Ukraine. He said that efforts must be made to promote dialogue and diplomacy to bring an end to the conflict. "The Deputy Prime Minister and I also understandably discussed some major global and regional issues. Notable among them was the war in Ukraine now in its fifth year. I think most of you would be aware that I myself have just come from Kyiv. India believes that endless wars must give way to an end to war. These are wars without winners. Every additional day means more deaths, more destruction, more loss to the parties themselves and more cost to the rest of the world," said EAM Jaishankar. –IANS ksk/as LATEST NEWS Rights group slams Pakistan for re-arrest of human rights lawyers hours after SC bail September 18, 2026 Ronaldo ends retirement speculation as Portugal name Nations League squad September 18, 2026 Women comprise over 40 pc of workforce in 57.8 pc districts in India September 18, 2026 US: Christians hold prayers for persecuted churches, imprisoned pastors in China September 18, 2026 Akanksha Chamola, Gaurav Khanna bump into each other but don’t speak at Ektaa Kapoor’s Ganpati celebrations September 18, 2026 FSSAI suspends licence of Paradise Distilleries over serious non-compliances September 18, 2026 India and UAE vow to deepen naval cooperation, maritime partnership September 18, 2026 India identifies 2,000 Indian residents in Nagoya as accommodation backup for Asian Games contingent September 18, 2026 CBI registers case against Anil Ambani, Reliance Capital in Rs 2,684 crore LIC fraud case September 18, 2026 Pakistan’s groundwater crisis driven by governance failures and policy paralysis September 18, 2026
